transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess I'm just having a hard time shaking some thoughts lately. I work as a financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and... I don't know, I've just been noticing things. It feels like certain people in the local arts and finance circles are... quietly tracking who I meet with. My clients, I mean. 

And... they do things. Like sending me little signals. Just through, you know, event invitations, or the topics they pick for panels... even who they decide to seat me next to at events. I keep telling myself it could all just be a coincidence, but... I just can't really let it go. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.

Can you tell me more about these signals you feel you're receiving? Do you believe these event invitations or seating arrangements are specifically meant to send you a message that others wouldn't understand?

Um... yeah. I guess so. Like I was saying, it just... it feels pointed. 

Other people probably wouldn't notice anything weird about a specific panel topic, or who gets put at my table. They'd just think it's normal networking. But... to me, it feels like they're letting me know they're paying attention to my business. To who I'm meeting with. 

I keep trying to tell myself it's just a coincidence, but... I don't know. I just can't really shake it.
Do you believe these signals are part of a deliberate and coordinated effort to communicate with you, or do you feel like you're noticing patterns that others might not see?

I... I don't know about coordinated. That sounds... I don't know. 

I just... I see the patterns. Like I said, the invitations, the panel topics... who sits near me. It's just... it's there. I try to tell myself it's just a coincidence, but... I'm convinced they're tracking my clients. I just... I can't let it go. I don't really want to talk about it much more than that.
Have you found yourself avoiding social events or feeling more isolated lately because of these concerns?

I guess... a little bit. I'm still working, but... I don't know. My practice has gotten smaller. 

I just... I avoid some of the public panels now. And sometimes I miss follow-ups with clients. It's just hard to... keep up the same level of contact I used to. So, yeah. I guess I've been pulling back.
Do you ever feel like these signals are part of a secret system that only you can understand, or that others would not believe you if you told them?

I don't... no. Not a secret system. That sounds... I don't know. 

And I haven't really tried telling anyone else about it, so... I don't know what they would think or if they'd believe me. I just prefer to keep it to myself.
Do you ever feel that these signals you're noticing are part of a larger hidden reality that others are unaware of, or that you have a special role or understanding in relation to them?

No... I don't think about it like that. 

I don't have any kind of special role. I'm just... trying to do my job, and I happen to notice these things. It's not some big hidden reality or anything like a movie... it's just what I see happening around my work. That's all it is.
Have you noticed any other types of unusual experiences or perceptions related to your work or interactions lately?
No... not really. Just what I already told you. I haven't noticed anything else.
Do you feel that the people sending these signals are trying to influence or control you in any way?

Control me? No... I don't feel like that. They aren't making me do anything. 

Like I said, I'm just doing my work... I just happen to see what they're doing. That's all.
Do you ever think that these signals you're noticing are part of a plan or scheme that others are keeping hidden from you, even if they deny it?

No... I don't think so. I mean... it's not a scheme or a plan. 

I'm just... I'm just doing my job and noticing things. That's all it is. I don't really know why it has to be a conspiracy or something. I just see what I see.
Do you ever feel certain that these signals you're noticing are real and true, even though others might not believe they exist?

Well... yeah. I mean, that's kind of why I came in. 

For a while now, I've just been... convinced. That certain people in the arts and finance circles here in Cincinnati are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. And they send me these little signals... through invitations, or the topics at panels, or even just who sits near me at events. 

Sometimes I try to tell myself it could just be a coincidence, but... I can't really let it go. I know what I'm seeing.
Even though you sometimes try to tell yourself it could be a coincidence, do you feel deep down that your belief about these signals is absolutely true and unshakable?

Yeah... I mean, like I just said... I can't let it go. 

I try to tell myself it's just a coincidence, but... I know they're tracking who I meet with. The invitations, the events... I know what I'm seeing. So... yeah. I am convinced it's real.
Even though you say you try to tell yourself it could be a coincidence, have you ever found any evidence that truly convinced you otherwise?
No... not really. I mean, I don't have, like, a piece of paper or an email to show you. It's just... I just know what I see.
Even though you don’t have any proof, do you feel completely certain that your belief about being tracked is true, and does it feel pointless to question it?

I... look, I feel like I just answered this. That's why I came in to see you in the first place. 

For a while now, I've just been convinced that those people in the arts and finance circles here are tracking my clients. The invitations, the panel topics... I try to tell myself it's just a coincidence, but I can't let it go. So... yeah. I'm certain.
Even though you say no one has confirmed this and you don’t have any clear proof, do you feel that trying to doubt or question your belief is pointless because you’re already sure it’s true?

Yeah... I don't really know how else to say it at this point. Doubting it doesn't change anything. 

The people here in Cincinnati... they're sending me signals. Even just... who sits near me at these events. It's not random. So, yes. I can't let it go. I'm sure.
Even though you haven’t found any proof and no one else has confirmed what you’re seeing, does it feel completely pointless to question your belief because you’re absolutely sure it’s true?

I... I don't know why we keep going over this. I feel like I'm just repeating myself. 

Yes. It feels pointless to question it. I told you, I came in because I'm convinced they're tracking my clients. The arts and finance people. The invitations, the topics, the seating... it's all signals. I try to say it's a coincidence, but... I can't let it go. I'm sure. Can we move on?
